summary: Q1 Explore review completed with changes-requested. 098 correctly identifies the excessive Agent-authored Run notes, missing input-reference preflight, retained terminal create-once invariant, formal artifact boundary, and legacy-compatibility limit. However, its selected provenance model still makes the Agent supply versionFingerprint for Core to verify, contrary to the updated reference's Core-owned generation requirement. It also assigns concrete focused/affected/full npm scripts to Q1 although the updated Q1 boundary freezes verification principles only and defers concrete scripts to F1. These two proposal-shaping errors must be corrected before Q1 can advance.

blockingFindings.title: The selected inputRef model preserves Agent-authored fingerprint authority
blockingFindings.evidence: Section 4.2 recommends option B: the Agent supplies inputRef.ref plus inputRef.versionFingerprint and Core merely verifies the supplied fingerprint. Section 4.3 then preflights that same Agent-authored value. The updated Q1 reference states that the production path must prohibit Agent-authored versionFingerprint: Core reads the real target, computes SHA-256, constructs ResultRef, and revalidates it before publish; the Agent may declare which result it consumes but cannot be the fingerprint authority (ref/01 section 6.5). The active manifest repeats that ResultRef/fingerprint is Core-derived and must not depend on Agent manual input. Current createRun accepts an unverified caller-supplied ResultRef, so choosing verification-only would retain the defect Q1 is meant to remove.
blockingFindings.impact: A stale, fabricated, or incorrectly computed fingerprint can still enter a new Run context through the production creation path. The later completion check only detects a subset of that problem after a malformed provenance record has already been persisted, so Q1 would not meet its Core-owned provenance acceptance boundary.
blockingFindings.requiredResolution: Replace option B and every dependent completion-preflight description with a Core-derived design. The caller may identify the consumed result/run, but createRun must resolve the actual result.json, compute and persist the canonical ResultRef itself, and reject a missing or invalid target before publishing the Run. Completion must recompute and compare the Core-created stored reference before terminal publication. Define the corresponding C1 delta and tests for successful derivation, missing target, replacement/mismatch, and pending preservation; do not retain an Agent-provided versionFingerprint as a production input.

blockingFindings.title: Q1 improperly takes ownership of concrete verification scripts
blockingFindings.evidence: Section 4.5 proposes adding npm run test:focused, test:affected, test:full, and verify:change in Q1. The updated reference sets Q1's scope to freeze the verification cost boundary only; its F1 section 8.3 assigns those concrete scripts to F1 and says their commands are frozen in the F1 Proposal. Q1's manifest outputs likewise name the focused/affected/full cost boundary, not a script implementation.
blockingFindings.impact: The Q1 Proposal would expand a corrective execution-model Change into F1's quality and verification-tooling work, creating an unnecessary cross-Change scope conflict and weakening the agreed staged Delivery plan.
blockingFindings.requiredResolution: Keep Q1's docs and delta requirements to the timing, ownership, and no-unauthorized-Full-Test principles. Remove concrete npm script creation from Q1's recommendation, required-file table, acceptance criteria, and tests. Record that F1 owns the command names, implementation, and script-level acceptance.
